estimationPercent.description: Percentage of the parent story's estimate assigned to this task (0–100). Requires estimation.strategy = 'percentage'.

condition.description: Condition evaluated against the parent story. Applied when this condition matches.

percent.description: Estimation percentage used when this condition matches (0–100).

estimationPercentCondition.description: Conditional estimation rules evaluated in order. The first matching condition's percent is used.

estimationFixed.description: Fixed Task Estimate in the Task's unit, independent of the Story Estimate. Written as supplied; percentage rounding and the minimum do not apply.

estimationFormula.description: Deprecated: formulas were never evaluated and give the task a Task Estimate of 0. Use estimationPercent or estimationFixed.
x-atomize-rules: Using this deprecated field produces a non-blocking warning, even in strict mode.

tags.description: Tags applied to the generated task.

condition.description: Condition evaluated against the parent story. If it does not match, this task is skipped.
x-atomize-rules: Offline Validation of a Template warns when this condition references custom fields; Online Validation is needed to verify that those fields exist on the platform.

dependsOn.description: IDs of tasks this task depends on. Atomize creates predecessor dependency links between these tasks.
x-atomize-rules: In a Resolved Template, dependencies must reference existing task IDs and must not form a cycle, including a dependency on the task itself.
A task with repeat set cannot have a non-empty dependsOn, and another task cannot depend on it, even when repeat is 1.
A task with dependencies should have its own id; validation reports a warning when it does not.

repeat.description: Number of identical Tasks to generate from this definition (default 1). Each copy's title gets its position, e.g. 'Review (2)'. Cannot be combined with dependsOn.
x-atomize-rules: When repeat is set, dependsOn must be absent or empty and other tasks cannot depend on this task, even when repeat is 1.
In a Resolved Template, repeat must not exceed validation.maxRepeat (20 by default). A Mixin defers this cap to the composing Template.

Every key must be a platform field reference in Namespace.FieldName format, such as Custom.ClientTier.

Azure DevOps single-line and multi-line text fields accept strings; only multi-line fields accept newlines. Boolean fields require booleans; decimal fields require numbers; integer fields require whole numbers.
Date/time fields accept ISO 8601 strings or supported macros such as @Today. Identity fields accept strings such as email addresses or @Me when supported by Azure DevOps.
Picklist values must match an allowed value and its string or integer type.

Offline Validation checks shape only. Online Validation verifies field existence, read-only status, types and allowed values; generation verifies them against live platform metadata before creating Work Items.
customFields.description: Azure DevOps custom fields to set on the task. Keys must be in 'Namespace.FieldName' format (e.g. 'Custom.ClientTier').

tasks.description: Task definitions that will be generated from this template.

taskType.description: Work Item type generated Tasks are created as, in the platform's own vocabulary (e.g. 'Task', 'Sub-task'). Defaults to Task on Azure DevOps. Online Validation checks custom fields and targetFields against this type.

strategy.description: Estimation strategy. 'percentage' distributes the parent story's estimate across tasks proportionally.

source.description: Story field that supplies the Story Estimate, as a platform field reference name (e.g. 'Custom.TShirtSize'). Replaces the platform's default fields with no fallback: a blank override is unresolvable. Azure DevOps defaults to StoryPoints, then Effort, Size and OriginalEstimate.

factor.description: Multiplier from the Story's unit to the Task's unit, e.g. 4 when 1 point = 4 hours.

x-atomize-rules: The conversion table must contain at least one entry.
table.description: Story Estimate value to non-negative Task-unit amount, matched exactly, e.g. { XS: 1, S: 2, M: 4, L: 5 } or { 1: 2, 2: 4, 3: 8 } for scales that aren't linear. A value missing from the table is unresolvable unless enabled multipliers match it; ifParentHasNoEstimation decides what happens next.

multipliers.description: Also accept a number followed by a table key, with optional whitespace: '0.3XL' or '0.3 XL' = 0.3 × XL. Defaults to false. Exact keys win; otherwise the longest matching suffix key wins. Forms such as 'XL*0.3' or '0,3XL' are unresolvable. Requires a table with at least one non-numeric key.
x-atomize-rules: When multipliers is true, conversion.table must be set and at least one table key must be non-numeric.

conversion.description: Translates the Story Estimate into the Task's unit before it is split across tasks. Set exactly one of factor or table; omit for one-to-one.
x-atomize-rules: Set exactly one of factor or table.
Rounding and minimumTaskEstimate apply after conversion and percentage distribution.

targetFields.description: Task fields that receive the Task Estimate, as platform field reference names. Azure DevOps defaults to Microsoft.VSTS.Scheduling.RemainingWork and Microsoft.VSTS.Scheduling.OriginalEstimate, with Microsoft.VSTS.Scheduling.CompletedWork initialised to 0. Overrides replace all default writes, including CompletedWork initialisation; values are written exactly as calculated.

normalize.description: What to do when the generated tasks' percentages don't add up to 100%. 'auto' (default) scales totals below 100% up and leaves totals above 100% as written unless you choose otherwise at generate time; 'always' scales to 100% in both directions; 'never' uses the percentages exactly as written, so a skipped task's share stays unallocated.

rounding.description: Rounding mode for percentage-based Task Estimates. Defaults to none, keeping decimal values. nearest rounds to the nearest half unit (0.5), up to the next half unit, and down to the previous half unit. Applied after conversion and distribution, before the minimum.

minimumTaskEstimate.description: Minimum percentage-based Task Estimate after rounding, in the Task's unit (hours on Azure DevOps). Defaults to 0. Takes precedence over deprecated minimumTaskPoints when both are set; fixed estimates bypass it.

minimumTaskPoints.description: Deprecated: use minimumTaskEstimate. Still honoured when minimumTaskEstimate is absent.
x-atomize-rules: minimumTaskEstimate takes precedence when both minimum fields are set. Using this deprecated field produces a non-blocking warning, even in strict mode.

ifParentHasNoEstimation.description: Behaviour when the Story Estimate is missing or cannot be converted. 'warn' (default) creates the tasks with blank estimates (never 0) and reports a warning, 'skip' creates no tasks for the Story and reports why, 'use-default' uses defaultParentEstimation instead. Without a defaultParentEstimation, use-default behaves like warn.

defaultParentEstimation.description: Story Estimate used when the real one is missing or cannot be converted and ifParentHasNoEstimation is 'use-default', in the Story's unit (e.g. 'M' or 5). Goes through the same conversion as a real Story Estimate.
x-atomize-rules: When ifParentHasNoEstimation is use-default and this value is set, it must be convertible: numeric without a table, or a matching conversion.table key (including enabled multipliers).

estimation.description: Global estimation configuration for all tasks in this template.

mode.description: 'strict' treats blocking validation warnings as errors; 'lenient' (default) allows warnings. Non-blocking advisories remain warnings in both modes.

x-atomize-rules: Choose one total constraint. If both are supplied, totalEstimationMustBe takes precedence and totalEstimationRange is ignored.
totalEstimationMustBe.description: Required total estimation percentage, counting each repeated copy. Validation checks that it is reachable between the lower and upper allocation bounds, including conditions and percentage overrides. It may exceed 100 when Tasks span roles.

x-atomize-rules: Choose one total constraint. If both are supplied, totalEstimationMustBe takes precedence and totalEstimationRange is ignored.
totalEstimationRange.description: Allowed total estimation percentage range, counting each repeated copy. Must overlap the lower and upper reachable allocation bounds, including conditions and percentage overrides. Bounds may exceed 100 when Tasks span roles.

minTasks.description: Minimum generated Task count the Template must define, counting each repeated copy.

maxTasks.description: Maximum generated Task count the Template may define, counting each repeated copy.

maxRepeat.description: Highest 'repeat' any task in this template may use (default 20). Raise it for a template that genuinely needs more copies.
x-atomize-rules: This cap applies to every task definition in the Resolved Template, including tasks contributed by Mixins.

min.description: Minimum allowed estimation percentage for a single task.

max.description: Maximum allowed estimation percentage for a single task.

taskEstimationRange.description: Inclusive bounds for each final task percentage after normalization, including percentage rounding. Fixed estimates are excluded.
x-atomize-rules: min must be less than or equal to max.

Checked after normalization and its percentage rounding, per repeated copy. With normalize: never, supplied percentages are used unchanged. Fixed estimates are excluded. Story-dependent conditions and percentage overrides are checked during preview and generation, once the active allocation is known. Task Estimate rounding in hours or points does not change this percentage constraint.

validation.description: Validation rules applied when this template is used.

category.description: Template category for discovery and grouping (e.g. 'Frontend', 'Backend', 'Infrastructure').

notes.description: Free-form context for the template's authors and maintainers.

examples.description: Deprecated: nothing in Atomize reads it. Describe when to use the template in description instead.
x-atomize-rules: Using this deprecated field produces a non-blocking warning, even in strict mode.

version.description: Template version this changelog entry describes.

date.description: Date of the change in YYYY-MM-DD format.

changes.description: Summary of what changed in this version.

changelog.description: Deprecated: nothing in Atomize reads it. Keep the template's history in version control.
x-atomize-rules: Using this deprecated field produces a non-blocking warning, even in strict mode.

metadata.description: Additional metadata for template discovery and documentation.

extends.description: Catalog Template name or file path of a parent Template to inherit from. Inherited fields such as name, filter, and tasks may be omitted.

mixins.description: Catalog Mixin names or file paths to compose into this Template. Resolved by the Template Library.

origin.description: Catalog ref (template:<name> or mixin:<name>) this template was derived from. Informational only — does not affect ref resolution.

formatVersion.description: Which edition of the Atomize schema this file follows. Currently "1.0"; omit it to mean "1.0". Not the template's own revision: that's version.
x-atomize-rules: Must be a format this release of Atomize can read: "1.0". Write it as a quoted string; an unquoted 1.0 is read as a number.

version.description: The author's own revision of this file, e.g. '1.2' or '2026-10'. Free text: Atomize shows it but never interprets it. A child Template does not inherit its parent's Revision.

name.description: Unique display name for this mixin.

description.description: What tasks this mixin contributes and when to include it.

id.description: Unique identifier for this task within the template. Referenced by 'dependsOn'.
x-atomize-rules: Non-empty task IDs must be unique within the file.

title.description: Task title — shown as the Work Item title on the platform. Supports Story variable interpolation.

description.description: Task description. Supports Story variable interpolation.

estimationPercent.description: Percentage of the parent story's estimate assigned to this task (0–100). Requires estimation.strategy = 'percentage'.

condition.description: Condition evaluated against the parent story. Applied when this condition matches.

percent.description: Estimation percentage used when this condition matches (0–100).

estimationPercentCondition.description: Conditional estimation rules evaluated in order. The first matching condition's percent is used.

estimationFixed.description: Fixed Task Estimate in the Task's unit, independent of the Story Estimate. Written as supplied; percentage rounding and the minimum do not apply.

estimationFormula.description: Deprecated: formulas were never evaluated and give the task a Task Estimate of 0. Use estimationPercent or estimationFixed.
x-atomize-rules: Using this deprecated field produces a non-blocking warning, even in strict mode.

tags.description: Tags applied to the generated task.

condition.description: Condition evaluated against the parent story. If it does not match, this task is skipped.
x-atomize-rules: Offline Validation of a Template warns when this condition references custom fields; Online Validation is needed to verify that those fields exist on the platform.

dependsOn.description: IDs of tasks this task depends on. Atomize creates predecessor dependency links between these tasks.
x-atomize-rules: In a Resolved Template, dependencies must reference existing task IDs and must not form a cycle, including a dependency on the task itself.
A task with repeat set cannot have a non-empty dependsOn, and another task cannot depend on it, even when repeat is 1.
A task with dependencies should have its own id; validation reports a warning when it does not.

repeat.description: Number of identical Tasks to generate from this definition (default 1). Each copy's title gets its position, e.g. 'Review (2)'. Cannot be combined with dependsOn.
x-atomize-rules: When repeat is set, dependsOn must be absent or empty and other tasks cannot depend on this task, even when repeat is 1.
In a Resolved Template, repeat must not exceed validation.maxRepeat (20 by default). A Mixin defers this cap to the composing Template.

assignTo.description: Email address or alias to assign this task to.

priority.description: Priority value for the generated task.

activity.description: Azure DevOps activity type for this task (e.g. 'Development', 'Testing', 'Design').

acceptanceCriteria.description: Deprecated: acceptance criteria are never written to the generated task. Move the text to description yourself; no removal quick fix is offered so the text is not lost.
x-atomize-rules: Using this deprecated field produces a non-blocking warning, even in strict mode.

acceptanceCriteriaAsChecklist.description: Deprecated: acceptance criteria are never written to the generated task, so this setting has no effect. Remove it.
x-atomize-rules: Using this deprecated field produces a non-blocking warning, even in strict mode.
Every key must be a platform field reference in Namespace.FieldName format, such as Custom.ClientTier.

Azure DevOps single-line and multi-line text fields accept strings; only multi-line fields accept newlines. Boolean fields require booleans; decimal fields require numbers; integer fields require whole numbers.
Date/time fields accept ISO 8601 strings or supported macros such as @Today. Identity fields accept strings such as email addresses or @Me when supported by Azure DevOps.
Picklist values must match an allowed value and its string or integer type.

Offline Validation checks shape only. Online Validation verifies field existence, read-only status, types and allowed values; generation verifies them against live platform metadata before creating Work Items.
customFields.description: Azure DevOps custom fields to set on the task. Keys must be in 'Namespace.FieldName' format (e.g. 'Custom.ClientTier').

tasks.description: Task definitions contributed by this mixin.

origin.description: Catalog ref (template:<name> or mixin:<name>) this mixin was derived from. Informational only — does not affect ref resolution.
